title: x
disposition: Endpoint ceilings now cache across public outputs as well as within one advance. Midpoint checks remain mandatory to avoid weakening resolution. Modal analyses have explicit private work counts; every solve/decomposition checks the unchanged wall deadline. budget.take continues counting adaptive trials, matching its existing public contract, rather than silently redefining the 512-attempt limit.

title: Wall-clock budget makes test flaky
disposition: Numerical/work-count and full waveform refinement tests now inject a deterministic elapsed clock, keep all error/residual/attempt guards, and are explicitly scoped as non-wall-rate evidence. Shared-service capture/reopen and ordinary/offscreen UI steps retain production clocks; forced-expiry tests retain atomic-refusal checks. No product time limit changed.

title: Silent no-op if RL load is missing or pin names differ
disposition: Static graph construction now checks RL replacement and rejects remaining RL.* endpoints explicitly. The positive inventory, compile, saved capture and browser tests also cover the actual graph.

title: Deadline atomicity check covers only x
disposition: Deadline test now compares x, capV, marshalled full result, proposal and cached ceiling after refusal.

title: Long-running refinement test not gated
disposition: Full 200 ms refinement remains in normal test gates, with an explicit testing.Short skip for intentionally shortened developer runs. Default validation does not use -short.

title: Aliasing assertion is tautological
disposition: Removed the scalar-alias assertion. The clone test mutates x and capV and verifies original storage is unchanged, while verifying step/ceiling values were carried.

title: Modal eigen-analysis repeated on every trial step
disposition: Intentional resolution checks retained. Cache already reuses accepted endpoint modes within/across outputs. A rejected trial at a different step size has different half/refined states, so caching only by step size is unsound; skipping midpoint checks could miss changed oscillation/growth rates. The whitelist excludes all hybrid controls, so no modal result is discarded by a hybrid-guard route. Work remains bounded, counted and wall-charged; positive production-clock public capture/UI controls pass. This observation is a performance tradeoff, not a reproduced correctness or budget-bypass defect.

title: mnaEquations failure ignored before mutating rows
disposition: False error-return premise: mixed.go mnaEquations explicitly returns ([][]float64, []float64); second value is the residual vector. It allocates a new denseMatrix on each call and does not cache it. Final source names both returns, validates dimensions/state shape and documents ownership. The independent series-RLC Jacobian test checks actual derivatives. No matrix alias/failure-return bug exists.

title: Discrete graph built then discarded for speaker example
disposition: Separated the two static example cases; the speaker case builds only its intended graph and defaults.

title: Deadline test may not exercise modal probing path
disposition: Clock now expires on the third probe check after two sensitivity-column solves; test asserts modalAnalyses>=1 and clockCalls>=3, then verifies complete atomic refusal.

title: Removed discrete Class AB production-clock coverage
disposition: The new graph is the exact prior fixture transformation: original 1nF graph, RL replaced by SP1 and VIN changed to 10mV; no compensation or bias change. Original resistor-loaded graph remains untouched. Separate SharedCaptureAndSavedExample plus ordinary/offscreen BrowserStepAndAgentParity use production clocks and require positive waveform progression; these do not accept a budget refusal as success.

title: Atomicity test ignores storage and proposal fields
disposition: The typed-deadline atomicity regression now also compares x, capV and both private proposal/cache fields, in addition to exact public result JSON.

title: x
disposition: Bounded, intentional resolution cost. Accepted endpoint mode is cached across outputs; every analysis is counted and charged to the unchanged wall deadline. Midpoint/endpoint mode checks are retained instead of skipping a potentially changing oscillation/growth rate. No demonstrated correctness defect remains; scratch-buffer/classification micro-optimization can be considered only with a measured bottleneck.

title: Modal Jacobian validity is logged but never asserted
disposition: Final test explicitly asserts storage/eigen validity, modal eligibility and a materially larger modal ceiling for the target circuit. Only this test changes after the complete final review; its focused race controls are rerun.

title: Test claims positive outputs without checking them
disposition: Renamed completed-output/work-count test to remove polarity ambiguity and now explicitly checks exact advanced time, speaker inventory and finite voltage/current. The separate full 200 ms refinement test already asserts both positive and negative >50mV output.
